issues.issue: Was she denied a fair opportunity to present her case because the Judge did not raise Canadianization at the interview?
issues.applicant_position: Judge breached procedural fairness by not raising Canadianization at the interview, so she could not prove it.
issues.respondent_position: Applicant had a fair chance; onus was on her, and the Judge had no duty to raise it at interview.
issues.result_quote: There is no obligation on the Citizenship Judge to raise the issue during the interview.

issues.issue: Did the Judge ignore or misapprehend evidence of her attachment to Canada before her US studies?
issues.applicant_position: Judge ignored the length and quality of her pre-study Canadian ties and her efforts to return; decided same day as filing.
issues.respondent_position: No evidence was shown to be ignored or misunderstood; the Judge need not mention every piece of evidence.
issues.result_quote: It is my opinion that the Citizenship Judge did take this evidence into account when he made his decision.

issues.issue: Did the Judge err in law by choosing the Pourghasemi test rather than the Papadogiorgakis/Koo mode-of-living test?
issues.applicant_position: Koo centrality-of-mode-of-living test is the principal test for students; the Judge erred by choosing Pourghasemi.
issues.respondent_position: No right or wrong test; the Judge properly applied one of the accepted tests.
issues.result_quote: I find that the Citizenship Judge did demonstrate in his reasons an understanding of the case law
